name: Image Alt Text
description: Measures the share of elements with non-empty alt text. Alt text is how AI crawlers and agents understand image content (and is an accessibility baseline), so missing alt leaves images invisible to them.
inputs: rendered DOM: every img element and its alt attribute

scoring.summary: Images with alt="" that are also marked decorative (role="presentation"/"none" or aria-hidden="true") are excluded. If no other img elements remain: 5. Otherwise percentage = round(100 * imagesWithAlt / totalImages), where an image counts only if alt exists and alt.trim() is non-empty. score = round(percentage / 100 * 5).

rules.condition: img has alt attribute with empty/whitespace value AND (role is 'presentation' or 'none' OR aria-hidden="true")
no img elements remain after excluding decorative images
img counts as having alt iff getAttribute("alt") !== null and alt.trim().length > 0 (plain alt="" and whitespace-only count as MISSING)

scoring.status_mapping: From the integer score with the shared rule: 4-5 pass, 3 warning, 0-2 fail. So 50-89% coverage is a warning or pass depending on rounding (e.g. 50% => 3 warning, 70% => 4 pass).

detect.source_procedure: Enumerate images that end up as on the evaluated page. Static HTML: every *.html (prioritise index.html and article/blog templates). Astro: src/layouts/*.astro plus src/pages/** (and src/content/** frontmatter feeding them). Hugo: layouts/** (baseof.html, partials/head*, single.html), hugo.toml/config.toml params, content/** frontmatter. Eleventy: _includes/**, _layouts/**, src/**, .eleventy.js, _data/**. Next.js app router: app/**/layout.tsx and page.tsx (metadata exports, JSX); pages router: pages/_document.tsx, pages/_app.tsx, in pages/**. Vite SPA: index.html and src/** components. Count: literal tags in HTML/templates/partials; Astro / from astro:assets (render , alt is required by the component); Next.js from next/image (renders ); Hugo images in layouts and markdown ![alt](src) rendered by Goldmark (markdown image alt becomes alt attribute; empty ![](x) gives alt=""); Eleventy eleventy-img shortcodes; JSX in React/Vue components; markdown/MDX content files for the page. For each, determine alt: literal non-empty string -> has alt; alt="" or missing -> missing; alt bound to an expression (alt={post.title}, alt="{{ .Title }}") -> treat as has alt unless the source value is clearly empty/undefined. Compute percentage and score per rules. Evaluate per page template (home plus a representative content page) and report per page; if a build output exists, parse built HTML instead.

parity.note: Literal templates and built HTML give exact parity. Differences arise from images injected by JavaScript (carousels, lazy loaders, third-party widgets, tracking pixels), CMS content images, components that conditionally render images, and dynamic alt expressions that may evaluate to empty strings. The extension counts every img in the live DOM including tracking pixels and widget images the repo does not contain.

fix_summary: Add descriptive alt attributes to each img in templates, components and markdown (e.g. ![Descriptive text](img.png), <Image alt="...">). The plugin can draft alt text from filename/context but a human should confirm. Purely decorative images should use alt="" together with role="presentation" or aria-hidden="true"; plain alt="" still counts as missing.

divergences.extension: alt="" always counts as missing, while the recommendation tells users to use alt="" for decorative images.
divergences.plugin: alt="" combined with role="presentation"/"none" or aria-hidden="true" is treated as explicitly decorative and left out of the count; plain alt="" still counts as missing, and the recommendation says so.
divergences.reason: Following the extension's own advice lowered the score; explicit decorative markup is the correct pattern.

divergences.extension: Status from the percentage: < 60% fail, < 90% warning (so 50-59% scores 3 but is a fail).
divergences.plugin: Status from the integer score with the shared 80% / 50% rule.

divergences.extension: Counts every img in the live DOM, including tracking pixels and widget images.
divergences.plugin: Counts img elements in each built/static HTML file.
divergences.reason: Source substitute: the plugin reads the repo, not a rendered page.
